stemMd: A committee must choose one painter and one engineer. There are 3 eligible painters and 4 eligible engineers, and no person belongs to both groups. How many pairs are possible?
explanationMd: Each of the three painters can be paired with any of the four engineers. Multiplying gives twelve distinct pairs. The roles distinguish the selections, and no overlap complicates the count.

distractorRationale.b: This adds group sizes instead of choosing one from each.
distractorRationale.a: This divides despite each pair having distinct roles.
distractorRationale.e: This counts the two role orders twice.
distractorRationale.d: This assumes four painters rather than three.
